description:
Track time against threads, billable and not, in hours/<Kind>/<Thread>.md.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD DESCRIPTION... [-m MINUTES] [-r RATE] [-c CURRENCY] [-d YYYY-MM-DD] [-t HH:MM] [--all] — append an entry.
  list [THREAD] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--json] — list entries.
  report [--thread T] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--json] — totals by thread and currency, unbilled time totalled separately.
  show ID [--json] — show one entry.
  edit ID [--description TEXT] [-m MINUTES] [-r RATE] [-c CURRENCY] [-d YYYY-MM-DD] [-t HH:MM] — change fields of an entry.
  rm ID [-y] — delete an entry.

Flags:
  log: THREAD is a thread name, 'Kind/Name', or wikilink; DESCRIPTION is one or more trailing words describing what was done. -m duration in minutes, default 60; -r hourly rate, 0 means unbillable; -c 3-letter ISO currency code, defaults to the thread's — with neither the entry is recorded as unbilled; -d date, YYYY-MM-DD, default today; -t time, HH:MM, default now; --all applies only to interactive capture.
  list: THREAD positional is optional; --since and --until are inclusive YYYY-MM-DD.
  report: --thread, --since, --until, --json.
  rm: -y skips confirmation.

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "DORA metric validation", "-m", "180"]
  ["log", "Topics/Running", "5k run", "-m", "30", "-d", "2026-09-10"]
  ["list", "Projects/SGB", "--since", "2026-09-01", "--json"]
  ["report", "--json"]

Notes:
  Calling `log` with no THREAD enters interactive capture and reads from stdin — always pass THREAD and a description.
  `rm` without -y prompts for confirmation and permanently deletes the entry.
  IDs are 8 hex chars, shared in one namespace with payments ids.
  An entry description is an invoice line item, not a narrative, and is not indexed by `search`. Put what actually happened in a log line via `buffer add-text`.
  Asking for a rate with no currency, on a thread with no currency, is refused.
  Every logged entry also drops a REF: into the buffer, filed under the work's date, which lands in the thread's daily log on the next `buffer flush`. This is best-effort; the entry is recorded either way.
